title: Eye-tracking accuracy across diverse populations
bottleneck: Eye tracking must work for all eye shapes, eyelid geometries, glasses, contact lenses, and lighting conditions, but accuracy degrades for many users: drooping eyelids, dark irises, and corrective lenses all confuse cameras. Foveated rendering and gaze interaction assume sub-degree accuracy that isn't guaranteed across the population.
why_it_blocks: Inconsistent eye tracking makes gaze-dependent features unreliable for large user segments, blocking accessibility and core rendering optimizations. A feature that works for only some users can't be a platform foundation.
current_state: Vendors claim high population coverage with improved algorithms and illumination, but real-world accuracy varies widely. Robust, calibration-free tracking for everyone remains aspirational. Calibration drift over a session means accuracy measured at setup does not hold, undermining gaze-contingent features mid-use.
